post.title: Your home went up $150K. Here's why that isn't profit
post.ig:
Your home's up $150,000? That's not your profit.
The Case-Shiller US home price index rose 82% from 2016 to 2025.
Our example: paid $300,000 in 2016, worth $450,000 in 2026. Selling at 6% costs $27,000; a $240,000 loan at 3.65% charges about $78,600 interest in 10 years. About $44,400 left (our math), before taxes, insurance and repairs.
And CPI rose 34% from 2016 to 2025.
Sources: S&P Case-Shiller and BLS via FRED, Freddie Mac, Redfin.
News and education, not financial advice.
